name: The manna hoarders
charge: Keeping manna overnight; going out to gather on the Sabbath
summary: Told to gather only a day's portion, some kept manna until morning and it bred worms and stank. Told there would be none on the seventh day, some went out to gather anyway and found nothing.
offense: The manna was given as a test and the terms of the test were stated when it was given: the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no (Exodus 16:4). The murmuring that preceded it, would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots (Exodus 16:3), was answered with the reminder that murmuring against the men the Lord sends is murmuring against the Lord: your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord (Exodus 16:8). Two failures followed and both were failures to trust a daily portion. Moses said, let no man leave of it till the morning, notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses, but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank (Exodus 16:19-20). Then on the seventh day there went out some of the people for to gather, and they found none (Exodus 16:27), though they had been told the day before that the sixth day's double portion was for the rest of the holy sabbath, and had been told to bake and seethe on the sixth day for it (Exodus 16:23).
judgment: The hoarded bread rotted and Moses was wroth with them (Exodus 16:20). The sabbath gatherers went out and found nothing, and the Lord answered them through Moses with the question that measures the whole wilderness: how long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws (Exodus 16:28), and the rule of the day was restated, abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day (Exodus 16:29). The sentences are small and exact, a stink and an empty basket, and they are recorded so that the sabbath and the daily portion would be understood before the greater tests came. An omer of the manna was laid up before the testimony, to be kept for the generations that would not see it (Exodus 16:32-34), so that the provision that proved them was kept as evidence.

verses.text: This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, according to the number of your persons; take ye every man for them which are in his tents.
And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.
And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.
And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.
Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.
And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.

And he said unto them, This is that which the Lord hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.
And Moses said, Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath unto the Lord: to day ye shall not find it in the field.
Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.
And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.
And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?
See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
So the people rested on the seventh day.
Give us this day our daily bread.
Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

entries.commentary: The whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots. The Lord commanded Moses to bring the people out, and when things got tough they made it his fault. That is us today. When the deliverance does not come easy, the people turn on the man sent to them instead of trusting the Most High who sent him.

Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no. The Lord proves His people by the daily portion. On the sixth day they were to prepare twice as much as they gathered daily; that word becomes important later in the chapter.

Your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord. Moses and Aaron were nobody of themselves; complaining against the leadership the Most High sets is murmuring against the Most High Himself. That is a heavy point for today. A man says he has no problem with the Bible, only with leadership, but it was the word coming out that made him mad; the Lord hears every murmur of the complainers and doubters.

At even the quails came up and covered the camp, and in the morning the manna lay like a small round thing, small as the hoar frost. They said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. An omer is a measure, a portion, like measuring cups of flour; every man gathered according to his eating, an omer for every man. He that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack.

Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning; some hearkened not and left it, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was wroth with them. They gathered it every morning, and when the sun waxed hot it melted; the portion was for the day the Lord gave it.

On the sixth day they gathered twice as much, and Moses said, Tomorrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake today. This is the scripture we always use to show that we do not cook on the sabbath; everything is prepared friday before sundown, and the leftovers are eaten the next day. What was laid up did not stink, neither was there any worm therein, because the Lord had given the bread of two days on the sixth day; the same manna that bred worms on other nights was preserved for the sabbath. Some of the people still went out on the seventh day to gather and found none, and the Lord said, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? The sabbath was already binding in the wilderness. Abide ye every man in his place on the seventh day is about not going out to gather food on the sabbath. Some foolish Israelites read verse 29 out of context and say you never have to leave your house or join a congregation on the sabbath; that is not what it says. The sabbath is a holy convocation, a large gathering, in all your dwellings, and we are to come together on it. For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

The house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: like coriander seed, white, and the taste of it like wafers made with honey. An omer is the tenth part of an ephah. Aaron laid up an omer of manna before the Testimony, to be kept for generations, that they may see the bread wherewith the Lord fed Israel in the wilderness. The manna that spoiled overnight on other days was preserved for generations; that is the power of the Most High. Israel ate manna forty years, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan. Stop reading over the power in these books with the colonizer's picture of the fathers in mind. Esau paints our fathers as a backward people in rags, but the Most High shewed mighty wonders through Genesis and Exodus; stop believing that image.

lawsResolved.text: Provide for food needed on the Sabbath in advance so it need not be gathered or bought or cooked on the Sabbath.

Six days of the week are to be used for labor, and the seventh day to be a Sabbath of rest in which you shall do no work. Exod. 16:22-30; Exod. 20:9-11; Exod. 23:12; Exod. 31:15; Exod. 34:21; Exod. 35:2; Lev, 23:3;
You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.
We are not to have a primary desire for earthly things.
